title: How to Make Claude Code Validate its work
summary: Amarildo Lucas compares a plain Claude Code run, handwritten validation rules, and Flowdeck’s harness on a SwiftUI weather-app bug. An iOS team can require screenshots, a named target, and an explicit list of performed and skipped checks before review; the shown harness report admits it ran no tests, and the article does not quantify handwritten-rule reliability or establish a controlled performance benchmark.
takeaway: Choose validation depth for the affected behavior, preserve the visual evidence, and read the report’s skipped checks; a built-and-launched screenshot does not establish test coverage.
